nfrs.requirement: BIC directory validation response < 500ms (p99)
nfrs.rationale: SWIFT BIC lookup is synchronous in the transfer entry form. Latency directly impacts form interactivity for PER-002.

nfrs.requirement: POST /international-transfers end-to-end API response < 2 seconds (p99) including account validation
nfrs.rationale: Channel makes a single blocking API call at initiation. Response latency > 2 seconds degrades portal user experience.

nfrs.requirement: SCA dynamic linking must bind to beneficiary IBAN, amount, and currency. SCA assertion must be validated by SVC-100 before PaymentIntent is created.
nfrs.rationale: PSRs 2017 Regulation 71 — dynamic linking is mandatory for payment initiation SCA. FIDO2 assertion must be bound to the specific payment parameters.

nfrs.requirement: SVC-010 POST /international-transfers availability >= 99.9% during SWIFT operating hours (06:00–18:00 UTC on SWIFT business days)
nfrs.rationale: Corporate clients operate within SWIFT operating hours. Unavailability during peak hours directly impacts revenue and client SLAs.

nfrs.requirement: FX pricing engine response < 1 second (p99)
nfrs.rationale: FX quote is synchronous and customer-facing. Latency degrades the transfer initiation experience.

nfrs.requirement: FX rate offered to customer must be within 5 bps of the bank's interbank rate at the time of quotation
nfrs.rationale: FCA Consumer Duty fair value obligation — FX margin must be proportionate. Consumer Duty evidence requires documented rate-setting methodology.

nfrs.requirement: Firm FX quote validity window: minimum 30 seconds for all amounts; minimum 120 seconds for amounts < £1M GBP equivalent
nfrs.rationale: Validity window must be adequate for PER-002 to review and accept without creating adverse FX risk for the bank.

nfrs.requirement: Sanctions screening per entity < 3,000ms (p99) — GOV-005-R02 hard limit
nfrs.rationale: OFSI screening SLA hard limit. Fan-out of up to 6 entities must complete in parallel; total compliance phase < 8 seconds (p99).

nfrs.requirement: Fraud scoring < 500ms (p99)
nfrs.rationale: Corporate wire fraud ML model P99 must match the retail FPS fraud scoring SLA to maintain consistent pre-execution check latency.

nfrs.requirement: Compliance checks fail-closed. If EVT-051 or EVT-052 is not received within 30 seconds of EVT-049 publication, the transfer is blocked pending manual review. No transfer may proceed without a confirmed compliance clearance.
nfrs.rationale: OFSI and MLR 2017 require that transactions are not processed without sanctions screening. Fail-open behaviour (proceeding without a screening confirmation) would create regulatory liability.

nfrs.requirement: Sanctions screening must cover 100% of OFSI Consolidated List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU Consolidated List, and OFAC SDN List. List refresh latency < 4 hours from OFSI/UN/EU/OFAC publication.
nfrs.rationale: GOV-005-R02 — no gap in list coverage. Standard Chartered £7.5m OFSI civil penalty (2024) for name-matching failures demonstrates enforcement risk.

nfrs.requirement: SWIFT message assembly < 2 seconds (p99)
nfrs.rationale: Message assembly (routing table lookup, pacs.008 serialisation, UETR generation) is an automated step. 2 seconds allows for correspondent routing table query and XML serialisation latency.

nfrs.requirement: All pacs.008 messages must include: ISO 20022 LEI for corporate originator (mandatory from 1 May 2025); SWIFT purpose code from ExternalPurpose1Code; structured beneficiary postal address (mandatory from November 2026).
nfrs.rationale: GOV-003-R03 — CHAPS ISO 20022 Enhanced Data requirements apply to SWIFT CBPR+ messages from the same dates. Non-compliant messages will be rejected by the SWIFT network.

nfrs.requirement: gpi UETR must be a globally unique RFC 4122 UUID v4. Collision probability must meet SWIFT gpi scheme requirements.
nfrs.rationale: SWIFT gpi rules require UETR global uniqueness. Duplicate UETRs cause correspondent bank processing failures and SWIFT audit issues.

nfrs.requirement: SWIFT message submission to SAA < 5 seconds (p99)
nfrs.rationale: Submission is the final bank-controlled step. Latency beyond 5 seconds risks missing SWIFT operating session cutoffs.

nfrs.requirement: SWIFT submission retry policy: maximum 3 attempts with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s) before publishing TransferFailed (EVT-057) with failure_reason = internal_error
nfrs.rationale: Transient SAA connectivity failures should not result in immediate failure. 3 retries with backoff is consistent with the FPS retry pattern (SVC-009) and SAA Cloud SLA.

nfrs.requirement: BusinessAccount debit (SVC-005 consuming EVT-054) must be idempotent on transfer_id. Duplicate EVT-054 redelivery must not result in duplicate account debits.
nfrs.rationale: Event bus at-least-once delivery guarantee requires idempotency at the consumer. Duplicate debits would cause incorrect account balances and regulatory liability.

nfrs.requirement: gpi tracker status updates propagated to corporate portal within 60 seconds of gpi status update received from SWIFT
nfrs.rationale: SWIFT gpi's key value proposition to corporate clients is real-time payment tracking. 60-second latency is the maximum acceptable for corporate use cases.

nfrs.requirement: TransferCompleted notification dispatched to PER-002 within 30 seconds of EVT-056 publication
nfrs.rationale: Completion notification is the primary customer-facing SLA outcome signal. Timely notification is required for Consumer Duty evidence of proactive customer communication.

nfrs.requirement: gpi tracker webhook receiver availability >= 99.9% during SWIFT operating hours
nfrs.rationale: Missed gpi tracker webhooks result in stale transfer status — directly impacting customer experience and gpi SLA monitoring.

cross_cutting_nfrs.requirement: All InternationalTransfer events (EVT-049 through EVT-057) are classified as data_classification = financial. Events containing beneficiary PII (EVT-049, EVT-056) must also be routed to the WORM audit pipeline.
cross_cutting_nfrs.rationale: FATF travel rule requires immutable records of originator and beneficiary identity data. MLR 2017 Regulation 40 requires five-year retention of CDD records.

cross_cutting_nfrs.requirement: Full audit trail from transfer_id creation to terminal event (EVT-056 or EVT-057) must be reconstructable from SVC-103 logs within 2 business days of a regulatory information request.
cross_cutting_nfrs.rationale: FCA and OFSI have powers to request transaction records within 2 business days under MLR 2017 and Policing and Crime Act 2017.

cross_cutting_nfrs.requirement: SVC-010 must implement circuit breaker pattern for SAA Cloud connectivity. On SAA unavailability: transfers queue in pending_submission status; maximum queue age 4 hours before auto-rejection.
cross_cutting_nfrs.rationale: SWIFT operating sessions have hard cutoff times. Queued transfers beyond 4 hours risk same-day value date failure — customer would need to resubmit for next business day.

cross_cutting_nfrs.requirement: SWIFT pacs.008 message format is mandatory for all JRN-009 transfers. MT103 format must not be used for new transfers after CBPR+ cutover (22 November 2025). SVC-010 must reject any attempt to generate an MT103 at the service layer.
cross_cutting_nfrs.rationale: GOV-003-R03 and SWIFT CBPR+ mandate. Submitting MT103 after the coexistence period ended would result in SWIFT message rejection.

regulatory_slas.obligation: Transfer must include originator information (name, account number, address) and beneficiary information with every cross-border payment instruction. Information must accompany the payment through the entire chain.
regulatory_slas.sla: On every pacs.008 submission — no exceptions

regulatory_slas.regulation: OFSI Financial Sanctions — Policing and Crime Act 2017
regulatory_slas.obligation: If a designated person is detected, OFSI must be notified within 14 calendar days.

International EEA payments: funds must be available at payee's PSP by D+1 business day. Non-EEA payments: D+4 business days maximum (by agreement). Customer must be informed of execution time at initiation.
